Electronics town, smaller NDT base: SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 for Cedar Rapids job seekers

Cedar Rapids is home to a famous aerospace name, and that leads many candidates to expect a deep pool of aerospace NDT jobs. The reality is more modest, and it is worth knowing before you choose a course. Here is where aerospace NDT work does exist around the city, which certification scheme it usually sits under, and why most local NDT careers run on ASNT SNT-TC-1A instead.

Why the aerospace name does not mean many aerospace NDT jobs

Collins Aerospace, one of the area's largest employers, does electronics work in Cedar Rapids: it develops microelectronics for its own products and has been expanding production of components for military communications equipment. Electronic assemblies are proven mostly by electrical testing and workmanship inspection. The ultrasonic, penetrant and magnetic particle work that fills NDT job boards belongs to metal parts, castings, forgings and welds, and much of that hardware is made elsewhere. So the aerospace NDT openings here are fewer than the city's aerospace profile suggests, and they tend to sit at suppliers and repair shops rather than at the big campus.

Where aerospace NDT does happen in eastern Iowa

Metal-parts suppliers. When a shop machines housings, brackets or castings for an aerospace customer, that customer's purchase order may carry a quality clause invoking NAS 410, or EN 4179 on European work. The clause flows down to whoever inspects the parts, and penetrant is often the main method. A NAS 410 shop names its Responsible Level 3 (RL3) in writing, and that person approves the written practice every inspector is certified to.

Aircraft maintenance and repair. The FAA leaves NDT personnel certification to the employer, and AC 65-31B accepts several standards, NAS 410, ATA Specification 105 and SNT-TC-1A among them, while a repair station follows whichever standard its own manual and its customers' contracts name. Small maintenance shops may buy NDT from an outside contractor rather than certify their own people.

Most local NDT jobs sit under SNT-TC-1A

Grain, corn and food processing plants are steady NDT customers around Cedar Rapids. Plants of that kind run boilers, pressure vessels, steam lines and storage, inspected to ASME and National Board rules. Fabricators and steel erectors work to AWS. If NextEra's restart of the Duane Arnold Energy Center near Palo wins NRC approval, nuclear in-service inspection will follow ASME Section XI and the ASNT documents that code references. All of these call for personnel certified by their employer under a written practice built on SNT-TC-1A, or the CP-189 standard where a code requires it. Most Cedar Rapids technicians will hold SNT-TC-1A certifications for most of their careers and meet NAS 410, if at all, on a supplier job.

A checklist before you accept an aerospace NDT job around Cedar Rapids

  1. Ask which document the written practice follows: NAS 410 and its revision (Revision 6 was released in December 2025), EN 4179, SNT-TC-1A, or a maintenance manual.
  2. Ask who the RL3 or Level 3 is, and whether that person is an employee or an outside agency.
  3. Ask which of your existing records will be credited. Under NAS 410 that is the RL3's call, and an SNT-TC-1A certificate is evidence rather than a qualification in its own right.
  4. Ask what formal training you still need. Penetrant and magnetic particle are where most people come up short, since the formal training NAS 410 expects in those two methods exceeds what SNT-TC-1A recommends.
  5. Ask whether the shop holds Nadcap AC7114 accreditation for the method, because auditors will trace your certification back to its evidence.
  6. Keep copies of course outlines with hours, your signed experience log, examination results and vision records. Certification ends when the job ends; the paperwork does not.

Small suppliers receiving a first NAS 410 purchase order can use our NAS 410 audit documentation support: Atlantis prepares and reviews the records and documents, and the company's own RL3 approves them.

Where Atlantis fits for Cedar Rapids

Most of the work in this market is plant, fabrication and supplier inspection, and that is what Atlantis training, built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, is designed for. Study the theory online whenever your shifts allow and put questions to our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT), rehearse in the Practical NDT simulator, and complete the hands-on part and the practical examination at your employer's plant under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Cedar Rapids. Newcomers usually begin with NDT Level 1 training, and supplier inspectors with penetrant testing training. Aerospace employers can have us draft written practices based on SNT-TC-1A that reflect customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to eastern Iowa suppliers. An Iowa supplier's RL3 decides whether outside coursework is credited toward a NAS 410 certification, so ask before enrolling. The NAS 410 and SNT-TC-1A comparison explains the rest.
